Subject: Clarify VAT handling for Q2 subcontractor pass-through fees

Hi Kimberly,

We're finalising the invoice for Q2 and noticed the line item for subcontractor pass-through fees (EUR 38,450). Our accounting team flagged that we need to confirm whether Redwood will treat this as reverse-charge (Clearwater as the recipient) or if Redwood will self-bill. Clearwater is VAT-registered in Hungary (HU12345678) and the subcontractor is based in Poland (PL987654321).

Can you confirm:
- Whether you will apply reverse-charge and issue an invoice net of VAT?
- If you need our VAT registration certificate (attached) or any additional evidence?
- Any changes to the invoice beneficiary (we currently bill to Clearwater Systems GmbH EU branch) that would affect bank routing?

I attached our VAT cert and a draft invoice. If easier, happy to jump on a quick call.

Thanks,
Anna
Billing Lead
Clearwater Systems

Hi Anna — thanks for the clear write-up and the VAT cert. Looping in Ben (billing ops) and Rishi (tax) to confirm the routing.

Preliminary:
- Our standard approach for subcontractor pass-throughs where the customer is VAT-registered in the EU is to apply reverse-charge (invoice net) when the customer provides a valid VAT ID and the supply is B2B.
- We'll need a copy of the subcontractor's Polish VAT registration or an invoice from them showing their Polish VAT number for our audit trail.
- Please confirm the legal invoicing entity you want on the final invoice (Clearwater Systems GmbH EU branch vs Clearwater Systems Ltd). If you're keeping the GmbH branch, include the local billing address and remittance details so our AR team can validate bank routing.

Ben/Rishi — can you confirm if any additional documentation is required for a reverse-charge treatment in this cross-EU scenario and whether Redwood needs to self-bill in any case?

Best,
Kimberly Park
Head of Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

Kimberly / Anna — quick operational note from billing ops:

- We can issue the invoice net of VAT under reverse-charge provided we have both buyer VAT (Clearwater HU12345678) and supplier VAT (Polish subcontractor PL987654321) on file. That satisfies our documentation for tax and audit.
- Preferred evidence: supplier invoice + supplier VAT registration screenshot (govt portal) or EU VIES confirmation. Supplier invoice alone is sometimes accepted but we prefer a registry lookup.
- Bank routing: if Clearwater wants funds sent to a different beneficiary name, we need a signed remittance instruction from an authorised signatory.

Action items for Anna: please upload the subcontractor VAT screenshot and indicate the legal invoice recipient. Once we have that, I'll mark the invoice as reverse-charge and re-issue.

Ben Carter
